top_story.headline: Mercury Public Affairs posts seven second-quarter lobbying terminations in a single batch
top_story.dek: The terminations all list a June 30, 2026 end date, about four months before they appeared in the LDA database.
paragraphs: Mercury Public Affairs, LLC had seven 2nd Quarter terminations posted since November 1, each with a termination date of June 30, 2026. They cover Better Schools for a Better Future ($70,000), CADA Energy, Inc ($40,000), Elanco US Inc. ($60,000), Grup Immobiliari Cierco ($100,000), Jeffer Mangels Butler & Mitchell LLP on behalf of Dateline Resources Limited ($40,000), Keystone Strategic Advisors on behalf of Batric Radunovic ($120,000) and SEMI Global ($30,000). Together they report $460,000 in income.

Quarterly lobbying reports are due 20 days after the quarter ends, so these filings appeared well after the deadline for a June 30 termination. The input does not show original filing dates, so the dates when they were first submitted are not confirmed here. The filings include former Sen. David Vitter as a covered position on the education client and former Rep. Patrick Costello (a congressman from 2005 to 2008, per the filing) on the rare earth elements client.

sections.headline: No new House or Senate disclosures in the input
paragraphs: The input contains no House or Senate financial disclosures filed since October 30 that earlier editions had not already reported. The Senate eFD fetch failed with an error, so Senate coverage for this window is unverified. The absence of Senate filings should not be read as confirmation that none were made.

sections.headline: Eight new registrations, nine terminations, and a batch of Mercury Public Affairs clients ending
paragraphs: LDA filings posted since November 1 total 58: 19 3rd Quarter reports, 14 3rd Quarter reports with no activity, 8 registrations, 7 2nd Quarter terminations, 5 3rd Quarter amendments, and 1 each of 4th Quarter termination (no activity), 4th Quarter report (no activity), 4th Quarter termination, 2nd Quarter amendment and 2nd Quarter report.

The table lists every registration and termination plus six activity reports with notable covered positions or subject matter. A further ten reports from The Majority Group, LLC are summarized below the table. The other 25 activity reports are left out.

rows: Critical mineral development; chemical manufacturing regulation.
Promoting economic stability and integration between the U.S. and Switzerland. Covered positions: Brian Gaston, Ethan Holmes, Patricia Engle, Paul Poteet, Rachel Alexander.
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services oversight for community-based care; Medicaid appropriations; FY2028 congressionally directed spending and community project funding.
Legislative prospects and policy changes in administration and spending for federal programs. Covered positions: Christopher Jaarda, Ed Perlmutter, Joshua Odintz, Yasmin Nelson.
National defense and appropriations issues. Covered positions: Aria Austin, Marissa Serafino, Mike Wakefield, Sean McGlynn.
Domestic manufacturing issues. Covered position: Matthew Flynn (former Deputy Assistant to the President and Acting White House Cabinet Secretary, per the filing).
Inox Solar Americas, LLC (new registration; foreign entities: Amura Renewables Private Limited, Inox Clean Energy Limited, Devansh Jain and Avarna Jain)
Section 232 polysilicon proclamation onshoring plans. Covered position: Cara Morrow.
Congressional and Department of War engagement on military missions and installations in Nebraska.
Lockheed Martin Aeronautic Sector (4th Quarter termination, no activity, $11,645 income, terminated 2026-10-31)
Better Schools for a Better Future (2nd Quarter termination, $70,000)
Charter school education and tax credits. Covered position: David Vitter.
Jeffer Mangels Butler & Mitchell LLP on behalf of Dateline Resources Limited (2nd Quarter termination, $40,000)
Rare earth elements. Covered position: Patrick Costello.
Keystone Strategic Advisors on behalf of Batric Radunovic (2nd Quarter termination, $120,000)
A decentralized financial platform. Covered positions: former Rep. Cheri Bustos and Jonathan Pyatt.
Technology and raising awareness of key products. Covered position: Cheri Bustos.
Artificial intelligence policy. Covered positions: Cheri Bustos, Jonathan Pyatt.
Loan guaranty facility agreement for partial guaranty of loans supporting U.S. and U.S.-aligned middle market businesses in Western Hemisphere supply chains.
A multi-state water infrastructure and flood control initiative. Covered position: former Rep. John Doolittle.

blocks.text: The Majority Group, LLC filed ten 3rd Quarter reports, each listing former congressional staff as covered positions (Bradford Cheney, Robert Ellsworth and/or Anne Canfield). The clients are Connected Commerce Council ($225,000), CBC National Bank Mortgage ($150,000), Nestidd ($125,000), The Amherst Group, LLC ($60,000, single-family rental housing and Executive Order 14376), Developers Alliance ($45,000), T-Mobile USA Inc ($30,000), Nationstar Mortgage ($30,000), United Fidelity Funding Corporation ($30,000), AI Salon ($30,000) and Click N' Close (no amount shown). 25 other activity reports were left out as routine or without a signal.
